differences.why: the study's constraints are mechanically decidable: the pipeline is model response -> deterministic verifier -> compliance outcome, and the verifier's output IS the outcome. There is no latent quantity an external rater estimates, so an agreement rate measures the rater. v4r3's development record shows what it measured: human and LLM reviewers introduced counting, arithmetic, segmentation, threshold and convention errors of exactly the kind the instrument exists to remove

wording_review.criterion: every model-facing wording exposes the comparison direction of the predicate that scores it, either by naming an operator from the registered direction lexicon or by a construction registered as entailing one and admissible for that operator. A wording that gives only a target quantity fails. An awkward-but-unambiguous wording does not block and is recorded rather than fixed: changing a live wording invalidates every measurement taken under it (§10.7 A')

requirement_verb.derivation: a requirement verb is a necessity operator over the counted feature: an answer that needs q of something still needs q of it when it has more, so `necessary(S = q)` and `S >= q` select the same answers. The converse reading, `S == q`, would require the verb to forbid a further occurrence, and no requirement verb does: `needs at most` is a contradiction, not a redundancy
